## What I did

This Next.js 16 canary integrates React's `<ViewTransition>` component (imported directly from `'react'`), gated behind an experimental flag — I followed the bundled guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/view-transitions.md`.

- **`next.config.ts`** — enabled `experimental.viewTransition`.
- **Shared element morph** — the grid thumbnail in `app/ProductGrid.tsx:15` and the detail hero in `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx:46` are both wrapped in `<ViewTransition name={`product-image-${slug}`} share="morph">`. React matches the names across routes and animates size/position automatically; the `morph` class gets a 400ms duration and a subtle mid-flight blur in CSS to hide interpolation artifacts. The hero sits outside the Suspense boundary (as the existing page already had it), so it's available immediately for the morph while the text details stream in.
- **Directional slides** — a new shared `app/PageTransition.tsx` wraps each page and maps transition types to animations. Grid → detail links carry `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}` (content slides left), and the "← Back to products" link carries `nav-back` (slides right). The `default: 'none'` mapping keeps untyped transitions (initial loads, browser back button) from sliding — though the image morph still plays on browser back since it's name-matched.
- **Suspense reveals** — on both the home grid and the detail info, the skeleton fallback is wrapped in `<ViewTransition exit="slide-down">` and the content in `<ViewTransition enter="slide-up" default="none">`, with asymmetric timing (fast 150ms exit, gentler 210ms delayed enter) so the skeleton hands off to the real content instead of popping.
- **Reduced motion** — a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` block in `app/globals.css` zeroes all view-transition animation durations and delays, so content swaps instantly (the browser default) for users with motion sensitivity.

One note: I added a root `react-canary.d.ts` with `/// <reference types="react/canary" />` — `ViewTransition` ships in `@types/react`'s canary types, so this is required for the type-check to pass (verified clean with `tsc --noEmit`).
